recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片被大量中型、細緻染色質、N:C 比高、部分可見核仁的芽細胞（blast）佔據，夾雜少數成熟嗜中性球與小淋巴球；此視野主要呈現急性骨髓性白血病成分，典型漿細胞並不明顯。
features: Sheets of medium to large blasts with high N:C ratio and scant to moderate pale blue cytoplasm
Round to slightly irregular nuclei with fine, dispersed chromatin and occasional small nucleoli
No obvious Auer rods or coarse granules in blasts at this magnification
Scattered mature neutrophils and small lymphocytes with markedly reduced normal hematopoiesis
Distinct plasma cells with eccentric nuclei and perinuclear hof are not clearly identified in this field
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear is highly cellular and dominated by a population of medium to large blasts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, finely dispersed chromatin, occasional nucleoli, and scant agranular basophilic cytoplasm. Residual maturing neutrophils and small lymphocytes are present, while erythroid and megakaryocytic elements are sparse. A distinct neoplastic plasma cell population is not evident in this particular field, so the plasma cell myeloma component must be documented on other fields, flow cytometry, or biopsy. Findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia in the given clinical setting of multiple myeloma (possibly therapy-related).

ddx.vs: Plasmablasts have more basophilic cytoplasm, eccentric nuclei with a central prominent nucleolus and are CD138/cytoplasmic light-chain positive but CD34/CD117/MPO negative.
Lymphoblasts are often smaller with scantier cytoplasm and are MPO negative with TdT and CD19 or CD3 expression by flow cytometry.
Recovering marrow shows synchronous maturation with promyelocytes and myelocytes rather than a monotonous blast population of at least 20%.
